fixture.name: slow_only_on_open_ended
fixture.why: Slower on open-ended questions than factual ones, which is how most people answer. Must stay silent.

expected_note: Originally a timing fixture. Timing analysis was removed; this transcript is retained as a negative control for contradiction detection. Nothing in it is self-inconsistent, so the expected output is an empty list.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What database were you using?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: MySQL, with a read replica for analytics.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Which cloud provider?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: AWS, all of it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How long were you there?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Three years and two months.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What was your title?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Senior software engineer, promoted from mid-level in year two.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me about a system you designed end to end.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The notification service. I wrote the design doc, got it reviewed by two staff engineers, and built it with one other person over about a quarter.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Describe a time you improved something nobody asked you to improve.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Our test suite took nineteen minutes. I spent two Fridays on it and got it to six by parallelising and killing some sleeps.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me about working with a difficult stakeholder.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A director who kept changing the acceptance criteria. I started sending a one-paragraph summary after every meeting and the changes mostly stopped.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Walk me through your most recent incident.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A memory leak in a consumer that only showed up under a particular retry pattern. We restarted on a timer for two days while I found it.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What do you think makes a codebase hard to work in?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Mostly it is when you cannot tell what is load-bearing. Not the size of it, the not knowing what you are allowed to change.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How do you think about technical debt?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: As a decision that somebody made with less information than we have now. That framing makes it easier to talk about without blaming anyone.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What would you change about how your last team worked?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We reviewed code well and designs badly. Most of our expensive mistakes were agreed to in a meeting nobody wrote down.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What kind of engineer do you want to be?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The one people bring the ambiguous problem to. I am less interested in being the fastest implementer.
